chapters.text: Getting outside sounds easy, until nobody can agree on what comes next. SideQuest gives that stuck moment a starting point for everyone. Here are our four family profiles, including two kids; their interests will help shape the adventure.

First we name the thing holding us back. Some days, we're tired. Today, our kids don't want to go, so we choose that challenge and ask for a playful start. The mission should tempt them to move, not nag them. We give ourselves an hour: enough time for a real outing, but small enough to feel possible. And we keep it within walking distance, close to home. A short route makes the first step feel smaller, even when motivation is low. With those choices made, the quest can begin.

I press Get Us Out. Gemma uses our choices to shape a quest right here on this computer. The family details become a story instead of another list of suggestions. I can cancel a long wait; today, we let the idea unfold.

A puzzle quest arrives on one card. Five connected objectives lead the children through the outing, with a bonus if they want to explore a little more. The highlighted main objective gives them a photo moment that belongs to this mission. Each step gives us a reason to keep going. When the card is ready, we can print it on A4 or take a picture of the screen. The mission goes with us; the screen can stay at home. What happens next belongs to us, out in the real world.

Later, we come home, and the mission is still waiting. No uploads, no proof: we simply say what happened. It is a quiet check-in, not a test. We only need to answer a couple of questions. We mark it complete, tick the bonus, and rate the outing Great. That honest answer helps the next quest fit our family better. The photo, if we took one, stays ours.

Back on the screen, the reward belongs to everyone: four hundred experience points each. The progress bars rise. Kid 2 and Mom cross into a new level, opening more kinds of adventures. We can see that time outside counted for every person who came along. A moment later, the next setup shows our family a little further along. SideQuest remembers our levels and what we rated highly, so the next mission can build on this one instead of starting from scratch. That history is a gentle nudge toward variety.

We ask for another mission, and now SideQuest has a stronger sense of what this family enjoys. Our recent rating and new levels join the children's interests as Gemma shapes the next card. It already knows what worked for us. This time, football leads the way. The quest guides us toward goalposts, then turns that place into the scene for its main photo objective. The picture will mark what we actually found. It feels like a new chapter of the same family story.
One card to carry, one reason to step outside. Now the screen can rest; our real adventure can begin.
